name: How do I decide between spot repairs and a full gut renovation on a foreclosure?

mainEntity.name: How do I decide between spot repairs and a full gut renovation on a foreclosure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing between a targeted repair and a full gut remodel comes down to the extent of hidden moisture damage, pest intrusion, and the condition of interior surfaces. If drywall is waterlogged, moldy, or heavily breached by vandalism, stripping rooms to the studs is often faster and more cost-effective than patching dozens of individual holes. A gut remodel also lets you correct outdated floor plans, reinforce framing, and run new wiring cleanly. If wall framing and subfloors remain plumb, dry, and structurally sound, targeted patching, surface prep, and new finish carpentry offer substantial cost savings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a full gut renovation if drywall has widespread water damage or heavy vandalism; opt for spot repairs if framing, subfloors, and walls remain dry and stable.
